correctness.rationale: Exact conditional probability for a prescribed fixed point and length-four pattern follows by selecting smaller/larger labels without replacement; off-window fixed points are independent of a given local order. Vandermonde summation yields a boundary-exclusion formula. The 24 proposed quadratic numerator identities reduce to 24 cubic polynomial identities; four exact evaluations at n=4,5,6,7, combined with the proven cubic degree bound, prove all n>=4. Displayed factorization and quadratic discriminants establish the three strict sign changes and all zeros. The standalone checker passed 954 exact assertions, including independent exhaustive enumeration of 46,224 permutations; enumeration does not substitute for the degree proof.

originality.rationale: The statement is an exact 24-pattern mixed covariance classification, including the 17-to-18 sign reversal for the self reverse-complement pattern 3142. The consulted primary sources address (respectively) fixed points/descents in double cosets, consecutive-pattern CLTs in restricted families, peak counts in conjugacy classes, or expected distinct consecutive patterns. Their inspected claims do not imply the 24 finite mixed moments. Published summaries of fixed-point/descent covariance and pattern frequency polytopes also do not imply this tensor. Historical priority is not proved; implicit general generating-function derivations remain a concrete risk.
residual_risks: Some highly relevant works were inspected only in specified portions rather than read fully; undiscovered appendices may contain equivalent moments.

value.rationale: All 24 natural four-consecutive-order statistics are classified simultaneously against the global fixed-point count. The boundary-exclusion identity explains all effects, and three genuine finite-size sign reversals include a delayed threshold at n=18 for 3142. A complete sign diagram in a natural small dimension is mathematically useful for finite permutation-model dependence and possible joint diagnostics, beyond a renamed statistic or isolated arbitrary parameter. No paper-scale application or independent certification is claimed.
